206600.name: Town Line

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies McKnight's Gap Road.

206600.description:
A weathered post marks the town line, its lettering scoured by rain
until only a few strokes remain. A lane climbs north toward the Dusty
Road and the tollhouse there, past an iron-barred gate whose chain now
hangs loose and open. Weeds grow thick in the verge, and the town lies
behind you to the west. Nobody has come this way in a long time, and
nobody seems to be leaving.

206601.name: McKnight's Gap Road

north.description: To the north lies Souvenir Shop.

east.description: To the east lies Town Line.

south.description: To the south lies Hardware Store.

west.description: To the west lies McKnight's Gap Road.

206601.description:
Two shopfronts face each other across the road here, the souvenir shop
to the north with painted wooden trinkets in its window and the hardware
store to the south with its shutters half drawn. A sign above each door
swings gently, though there is no wind. The road runs east to the town
line and west back toward the heart of town. Gravel crunches under every
step, loud in the silence.

206602.name: Souvenir Shop

south.description: To the south lies McKnight's Gap Road.

206602.description:
Shelves of painted mugs, carved wooden bears and little tin spires crowd
this small shop, all of them furred with dust. A glass counter holds
picture cards faded nearly white, and a brass bell hangs above the door.
Something has gone through the back stock and left shards scattered over
the floor. The way out lies south, onto the road.

206603.name: Hardware Store

north.description: To the north lies McKnight's Gap Road.

down.description: To the down lies The Cellar.

206603.description:
Narrow aisles of nail bins, coiled rope and rusted tools lead back
through the dim hardware store. A counter at the front still holds a
ledger and a scale, and shovel handles stand in a barrel like a bundle
of spears. Cold air breathes from a trapdoor at the back, whose steps
lead down into the cellar. The door to the road opens north.

206604.name: The Cellar

up.description: To the up lies Hardware Store.

206604.description:
The cellar is a low, damp room of fieldstone and packed earth, its
ceiling beams close overhead. Barrels of nails and crates of straw-
packed lamp glass line the walls, and a tangle of cord hangs in one
corner. A stair of rough planks climbs up to the shop. The air tastes of
mould and old iron, and the dark presses close beyond the lamplight.

206605.name: McKnight's Gap Road

north.description: To the north lies East Tudor Street.

east.description: To the east lies McKnight's Gap Road.

south.description: To the south lies Town Garden.

west.description: To the west lies McKnight's Gap Intersection.

206605.description:
McKnight's Gap Road is a hard-packed road rutted by wagon wheels, with a
plank walk running beside it. A tall hedge guards the garden gate on the
south side, which stands shut. The road runs on east toward the edge of
town and west to the intersection, while a side street turns north
toward the houses. Hitching rails stand empty along the walk, and
nothing has passed in a long while.

206606.name: East Tudor Street

north.description: To the north lies East Tudor Street.

east.description: To the east lies A Deserted Home.

south.description: To the south lies McKnight's Gap Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The Porch.

206606.description:
The street widens at the crossing with McKnight's Gap Road, which lies
just south, and a lamp post leans over a pitted kerb. An open door in
the east wall of the nearest house gives onto a deserted home with its
curtains hanging in rags. To the west a sagging porch looks out over the
street, and north the way runs back toward the square. A dog bowl lies
overturned beside the lamp post.

206607.name: A Deserted Home

west.description: To the west lies East Tudor Street.

206607.description:
Dust sheets hide the furniture of this small parlour, and a wall clock
has stopped at ten past three. Wallpaper curls from the corners in long
brown tongues. A cold supper sits on the dining table, black with mould
and set for four. The front door, the only way out, opens west onto the
street.

206608.name: On The Porch

east.description: To the east lies East Tudor Street.

west.description: To the west lies The Neighbor's House.

206608.description:
A wide wooden porch wraps around the front of the house, its rail loose
and its boards soft with rot. A rocking chair sits turned toward the
wall, and a wind chime hangs silent. Steps lead east down to East Tudor
Street, and the front door stands west, ajar on a dark hall.

206609.name: The Neighbor's House

east.description: To the east lies On The Porch.

west.description: To the west lies The Yard.

206609.description:
The kitchen is a tidy ruin: pots hang over a cold range, a plate sits
half-washed in a basin, and the table is laid for a meal that never
came. Curtains of heavy blue cloth are pinned shut over every window. A
back door opens west onto the yard, while a front hall runs east to the
porch. The air is stale and smells faintly of cloves.

206610.name: The Yard

east.description: To the east lies The Neighbor's House.

206610.description:
A narrow back yard of patchy grass lies behind the neighbour's home,
with a rusted swing and a washline hung with sheets that have gone stiff
and grey. Wild morning glories strangle the fence. A back door stands in
the house wall east of the grass, hanging ajar. Overhead, the vine you
came by sags toward the oak.

206611.name: East Tudor Street

north.description: To the north lies Summon Square.

south.description: To the south lies East Tudor Street.

206611.description:
East Tudor Street runs between two rows of neat clapboard houses with
deep porches and steps that nobody has swept in weeks. A porch swing
creaks on a single chain. Dead leaves pile against the doors, and a milk
jug on the nearest step has gone sour and green. The street leads north
back to Summon Square and on south past more silent houses.

206612.name: Summon Square

north.description: To the north lies The Morgue.

east.description: To the east lies The Town Church.

south.description: To the south lies East Tudor Street.

west.description: To the west lies Tudor Street.

206612.description:
Summon Square is the little heart of the town, a patch of worn cobbles
with a dry fountain and a bench nobody sits on. The church stands to the
east with its doors closed and its bell silent, while the low brick
morgue squats to the north behind a plain door. Tudor Street runs off
west, and East Tudor Street leads away south. Every window around the
square has its curtains drawn tight, though it is midday.

206613.name: The Town Church

west.description: To the west lies Summon Square.

206613.description:
Rows of dark pews fill the nave of the little white church, their
hymnals scattered and swollen with damp. Dust lies thick on the altar,
and the cross above it hangs crooked on a single nail. Coloured light
from a cracked window falls in broken pieces across the aisle. The door
lies at the back, west of the last pew, and it is the only way out.

6614.name: The Morgue

north.description: To the north lies Autopsy Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Freezer.

south.description: To the south lies Summon Square.

6614.description:
The morgue is a low tiled room that smells of lye, cold stone and
something sweeter underneath. Steel drawers line the far wall, a few of
them standing open and empty. A ledger lies on a desk, its last entries
scrawled in a shaking hand and then abandoned. The autopsy room lies
through a door to the north, a heavy door leads east into the freezer,
and the square waits back south.

extra_descs.ledger:
The ledger lists the dead of the town by date. In the last week the
names stop, and the final lines are only tally marks, many of them
struck through.

6615.name: The Freezer

east.description: To the east lies Back Freezer.

west.description: To the west lies The Morgue.

6615.description:
Cold bites the moment you step through the heavy door, and your breath
hangs before you in grey puffs. Rows of steel shelves hold long shapes
under stained sheeting, some of them fallen askew. A failing machine
hums somewhere behind the walls, and the floor is slick with old damp.
The morgue lies back west, and the room narrows toward a deeper cold in
the east.

6616.name: Back Freezer

west.description: To the west lies The Freezer.

6616.description:
The last of the cold rooms is little more than a closet of white-painted
steel, its shelves bent as if something heavy had thrown itself against
them. A handprint, brown and dry, smears the inner wall at the height of
a man's shoulder. The bulb overhead has burst and left only grey dark.
The only way out is west, into the freezer, and the cold follows you at
every step.

6617.name: Autopsy Room

south.description: To the south lies The Morgue.

6617.description:
A single steel table sits under a hooded lamp in the middle of this
bare, tiled chamber, its drain stained dark. Instruments are laid out on
a tray in a neat row, as if the doctor meant to return in a moment. The
air is chill and still, and the tiles sweat in the lamplight. The only
way out is south, back into the morgue.

6618.name: Tudor Street

east.description: To the east lies Summon Square.

south.description: To the south lies One Room School House.

west.description: To the west lies Tudor Square.

6618.description:
Tudor Street is the old main street, lined with brick shopfronts whose
signs have lost their paint. The little school stands to the south
behind a low iron fence, its bell rope motionless. The street runs east
to Summon Square and west to Tudor Square. Boards cover a few windows,
and a saucer of milk by one door has dried to a crust.

6619.name: One Room School House

north.description: To the north lies Tudor Street.

6619.description:
Rows of small desks face a blackboard still scrawled with a half-
finished lesson, the chalk worn to a nub on the ledge. A cold stove
stands in one corner beside a bucket of kindling, and a map of the realm
curls on the wall. The windows are shuttered against the day, and coats
still hang on pegs by the door. The only door opens north to the street.

6620.name: Tudor Square

north.description: To the north lies Doctor's Office.

east.description: To the east lies Tudor Street.

south.description: To the south lies West Tudor Street.

6620.description:
Tudor Square is a small cobbled place with a granite memorial at its
centre, its names half hidden under moss. The doctor's office faces the
memorial on the north side, its door painted green and shut tight. Tudor
Street leads off east, and West Tudor Street runs south. A pair of
benches face each other like quarrelling neighbours, and nobody has sat
on either.

extra_descs.memorial granite names:
The granite is carved with the names of the town's sons lost in the old
border wars. A newer name has been chiselled at the bottom, roughly, in
a hand that was not a mason's.

6621.name: Doctor's Office

south.description: To the south lies Tudor Square.

6621.description:
A small waiting room gives onto a cluttered consulting desk, where
bottles of coloured tonic stand corked in rows. The doctor's diploma
hangs crooked, and a bag of instruments yawns open on a chair. Bloodied
cloths soak in a basin, long since dried to rust. The door to the square
is south, behind you.

6622.name: West Tudor Street

north.description: To the north lies Tudor Square.

south.description: To the south lies West Tudor Street.

up.description: To the up lies The Treehouse.

6622.description:
A great oak stands beside the road, one thick limb carrying a ladder of
nailed boards up to a treehouse. Picket fences run to either side, the
whitewash peeling in long strips. The street leads north to the square
and south toward the intersection. Acorns crunch underfoot, and the
oak's shadow lies black across the road.

6623.name: The Treehouse

east.description: To the east lies On The Vine.

down.description: To the down lies West Tudor Street.

6623.description:
Rough planks make a floor among the great limbs, and leaves press at the
gaps between the boards. A rope-hung lantern, a tin box of marbles and a
child's drawing of a smiling sun are the only furnishings. A vine runs
from a window gap east and out along a branch. The ladder down leads
back to the street.

6624.name: On The Vine

east.description: To the east lies The Yard.

6624.description:
You are out on a thick vine strung from the oak across the gardens,
swaying above the weeds below. The bark of the branch is slick with
moss, and leaves whisper all around. The vine ends east at a patch of
grass, a little way down. The treehouse lies behind you.

6625.name: School Master's House

west.description: To the west lies West Tudor Street.

6625.description:
Books crowd every shelf of the schoolmaster's front room, and a lectern
holds a Bible and a heap of marked slates. A pipe lies on the arm of a
reading chair, still faintly sweet with old smoke. The curtains have
been nailed shut with long, bent nails. The door to the street is west,
and a feeling of being watched lingers by it.

6626.name: Abandoned House

north.description: To the north lies A Closet In An Abandoned House.

east.description: To the east lies West Tudor Street.

6626.description:
The front room of the abandoned house is bare of furniture but for a
rotted settee, and the floor has been scuffed by many feet. Plaster
hangs from the ceiling in wet strips, and scratches mark the doorframe
at knee height. A narrow door in the north wall opens on a closet, and
the front door lies east. A cold draught moves through the room,
smelling of damp earth.

6627.name: A Closet In An Abandoned House

south.description: To the south lies Abandoned House.

6627.description:
The closet is hardly wider than a man's shoulders, lined with bare
shelves and a hook or two for coats. Scratches and dark stains cover the
inside of the door. A tattered blanket is wadded in one corner, as
though someone hid here a long while. The only way out is back south
into the house.

6628.name: West Tudor Street

north.description: To the north lies West Tudor Street.

east.description: To the east lies School Master's House.

south.description: To the south lies McKnight's Gap Intersection.

west.description: To the west lies Abandoned House.

6628.description:
West Tudor Street passes between two old houses here: the schoolmaster's
home to the east behind a picket fence, and an abandoned house to the
west with its gate off its hinges. The road runs north toward the square
and south to the intersection. Ivy has pulled down part of a porch roof.
Ruts in the road dust show no tracks but those of the wind.

6629.name: McKnight's Gap Intersection

north.description: To the north lies West Tudor Street.

east.description: To the east lies McKnight's Gap Road.

south.description: To the south lies In The Covered Bridge.

west.description: To the west lies The Town Common.

6629.description:
Four ways meet at the intersection. West Tudor Street heads north
between tall elms, McKnight's Gap Road runs east, a covered bridge lies
to the south, and the Town Common opens west. A weathered signpost
points the ways, its arrows swinging loose. The elm shade is deep and
cool even at noon, and the leaves rustle with no wind to stir them.

extra_descs.signpost arrows sign:
The old signpost has three arrows, each hand-lettered: Tudor Street, The
Covered Bridge, The Common. Someone has scratched a fourth arrow into
the wood pointing toward the hill, and gouged out the name.

6630.name: Town Garden

north.description: To the north lies McKnight's Gap Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Hatch-Schell.

6630.description:
The town garden is a square of tended lawns gone to seed, with a stone
birdbath cracked down the middle and rose beds choked with weeds. Gravel
paths wander between benches whose paint has flaked to grey. A gate to
the north opens on McKnight's Gap Road, and the path runs south toward
the Hatch-Schell. The roses still bloom, dark red and heavy, in the
stillness.

6631.name: The Hatch-Schell

north.description: To the north lies Town Garden.

west.description: To the west lies Under The Bridge.

up.description: To the up lies The Cat Walks.

6631.description:
The Hatch-Schell is an open-fronted shell of curved timber standing on a
trodden clearing, like a bandstand, its plank steps scuffed by long-ago
dances. A ladder of iron rungs climbs up to the cat walks above the
stage. North, the garden path runs back to the lawns, and west a low
passage leads under a bridge. Bunting hangs in faded tatters from the
roof.

6632.name: The Cat Walks

east.description: To the east lies The West Walk.

down.description: To the down lies The Hatch-Schell.

6632.description:
A narrow plank gallery runs along the rafters above the stage, creaking
with every step. Ropes and pulleys hang here, with the stale smell of
old paint, and a rail of lamps sits dark. A ladder leads down to the
Hatch-Schell, and the walk goes on east. Dust shakes down in drifts.

6633.name: The West Walk

east.description: To the east lies Center Stage On The Walk.

west.description: To the west lies The Cat Walks.

6633.description:
The walk is only three planks wide here, with a thin rope for a rail.
Painted flats hang from the beams, showing a country village that looks
eerily like the town below. The planks run east on toward the centre,
and west they return to the ladder. A dead lamp swings by its chain.

6634.name: Center Stage On The Walk

west.description: To the west lies The West Walk.

6634.description:
The gallery widens into a little platform at the stage's centre, hung
with a velvet curtain gone moth-eaten and dark. A single stool stands
there with a prompt book open on it. From the platform you can see the
whole shell below and the empty benches beyond. The only path leads back
west along the walk.

6636.name: Under The Bridge

east.description: To the east lies The Hatch-Schell.

west.description: To the west lies The Thicket.

6636.description:
The ground dips beneath the dark underside of an old timber bridge,
where the beams drip and the stones are slick with moss. Initials are
carved into the posts, and a few rusted nails jut from the planks. The
Hatch-Schell lies back east, while west the way pushes into a tangle of
brush. A cold draught slides under the bridge, smelling of earth.

6637.name: The Thicket

north.description: To the north lies The Town Common.

east.description: To the east lies Under The Bridge.

6637.description:
Brambles and young birches crowd together here, their branches knitted
so tightly that daylight comes down in scraps. The ground is soft with
years of leaf mould, and thorny runners snag at your cloak. A trodden
path leads north to the Town Common, and east the dark underside of the
bridge waits. Somewhere in the undergrowth a twig snaps, and then there
is nothing.

6638.name: The Town Common

north.description: To the north lies Outside The Do-Drop Inn.

east.description: To the east lies McKnight's Gap Intersection.

west.description: To the west lies Look Out Point.

6638.description:
The common is a wide trampled green with a bare flagpole whose rope
slaps against the mast, and a pair of cattle troughs gone green with
slime. The Do-Drop Inn stands to the north, its sign hanging by one
chain. The way east returns to McKnight's Gap Intersection, and a rise
to the west climbs to Look Out Point. Beyond the grass, thorny scrub
shows where the thicket begins.

6639.name: Outside The Do-Drop Inn

north.description: To the north lies The Do-Drop Inn.

south.description: To the south lies The Town Common.

6639.description:
A covered porch runs along the front of the inn, with rocking chairs
lined up and tipped forward as though the sitters left in haste.
Lanterns hang unlit from hooks, and a notice board is thick with curling
papers. The inn's door stands north, and the steps lead south down to
the Town Common. The boards underfoot are damp with the night's dew.

6640.name: The Do-Drop Inn

south.description: To the south lies Outside The Do-Drop Inn.

up.description: To the up lies The Flight Deck.

6640.description:
The common room of the Do-Drop Inn is long and low, with a hearth gone
to cold ash and tables still set with half-drunk mugs. A fiddle hangs on
the wall above the bar, its strings slack. Rough stairs rise up to the
rooms and the flight deck, while the door south leads out to the porch.
The room smells of stale ale and shut-in air.

6641.name: The Flight Deck

north.description: To the north lies The Griffin Deck.

east.description: To the east lies The Dragon Deck.

south.description: To the south lies The Beetle Deck.

west.description: To the west lies The Pegasi Deck.

down.description: To the down lies The Do-Drop Inn.

6641.description:
A timber hall under the roof ridge holds the flight deck, with four open
archways leading out to the mounting platforms. Leather harnesses hang
from pegs, and straw and old feathers are scattered on the boards. North
is the griffin deck, east the dragon deck, south the beetle deck and
west the pegasi deck, while the stair goes down to the inn. A high
draught carries the smell of beasts long gone.

6642.name: Look Out Point

east.description: To the east lies The Town Common.

6642.description:
A bare knoll at the town's edge gives a view across the roofs, the
church spire and the fields beyond. An iron rail and a stone bench stand
at the brink. The house on the hill stands black against the clouds
across the valley, its windows catching a last light. The only path back
runs east to the Town Common.

6644.name: In The Covered Bridge

north.description: To the north lies McKnight's Gap Intersection.

south.description: To the south lies Lower Tudor St..

6644.description:
The old covered bridge is a long, barn-dark tunnel of weathered planks,
its floor booming hollowly with each step. Names and hearts are cut into
the walls, many worn smooth by hands. Gaps in the siding let thin bars
of light fall on the boards, and somewhere below, water mutters over
stones. The bridge leads north to the intersection and south toward the
lower end of Tudor Street.

6645.name: Lower Tudor St.

north.description: To the north lies In The Covered Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies The Corn Field.

6645.description:
The last houses of the town stand here, small and shabby, with their
back gardens already gone to corn. Wheel ruts run on toward the fields,
and a leaning lantern post stands at the end of the lane. The covered
bridge is behind you to the north, and the road gives way south into
rows of tall corn.

6646.name: The Corn Field

north.description: To the north lies Lower Tudor St..

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Corn Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6646.description:
Tall corn rises on every hand, its dry leaves rattling like paper. The
rows lead north to the last houses of Tudor Street, east to a pasture of
cropped grass, south into deeper corn, and west to another grazing
field. A heap of cornshocks leans against a rotten stake, bound with
twine. The stalks cut off the sky to a thin strip.

6647.name: The Corn Field

north.description: To the north lies The Corn Field.

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Corn Field.

6647.description:
The corn is thickest here, its leaves closing overhead and shutting out
most of the daylight. The ground slopes slightly down, and a low mound
of fresh earth rises between the rows, raw and unplanted. Paths lead
north toward the lane, east to a pasture, and west into more corn. The
stalks do not rustle, and the air is oddly warm.

6648.name: The Corn Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

east.description: To the east lies The Corn Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Corn Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6648.description:
The rows open into a crossing of paths where the corn has been flattened
in a ring. A pole stands in the middle with a cross-brace and tatters of
cloth, a scarecrow stripped of its coat. The corn leads south and east
into deeper stands, west to open pasture, and north the stalks give out
onto grass. Droppings whiten the pole, and the rags hang very still.

extra_descs.scarecrow pole rags:
The scarecrow's coat has been taken, and the pole is bound with fresh
twine. The knots are tied by someone who knew how, and the cross-brace
is stained at the ends.

6649.name: The Corn Field

north.description: To the north lies The Corn Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Corn Field.

6649.description:
A narrow aisle between the corn runs north and south, its floor hard
clay, its walls dry stalks that whisper together. A ragged cloth bag
lies in the dirt where someone dropped it in haste. The ears hang heavy
and unpicked, some already rotting black on the stalk. Little light
finds the ground.

6650.name: The Corn Field

north.description: To the north lies The Corn Field.

east.description: To the east lies A Red Barn.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6650.description:
The corn stands head-high around a trampled clearing in the rows. A red
barn looms to the east, its great door open a hand's width, and the
stalks lead north deeper into the field, south to a pasture, and west to
another. Crumpled leaves and snapped stalks mark where something heavy
has passed. The air is thick with the smell of ripe grain and damp.

6651.name: The Pen

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

6651.description:
The pen is a square yard of trampled mud walled by split rails, with a
feeding rack along one side and a gate at either end. Posts are scored
with old claw marks, and the rails are splashed with dried rust-brown
stains. A gate in the north leads to the grazing field, another south to
a second pasture. The ground is churned deep, as if a herd had been
driven round and round.

6652.name: A Red Barn

west.description: To the west lies The Corn Field.

6652.description:
Hay bales climb the walls of the great red barn nearly to the rafters,
and a loft ladder rots in its place. Slanting bars of light fall through
gaps in the siding onto a floor of pale straw. Farm tools hang in rows,
their edges bright and clean as if someone had honed them. The wide door
at the barn's side opens west to the corn.

6653.name: The Stable

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6653.description:
Empty stalls line the stable, their half doors splintered and the
nameplates scratched out. Old harness hangs from pegs, stiff with mould,
and a pitchfork leans in the corner. The straw is trampled flat, and
dark stains cling to the post at the end of the row. The wide door to
the yard lies west.

6654.name: The Grazing Field

east.description: To the east lies The Corn Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Corn Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6654.description:
The pasture here is bordered by a ditch choked with nettles and old
rainwater. A wooden stile stands over the ditch to nowhere. East the
field meets the corn, west it runs on toward more grass, and south a
rank of stalks stands like a wall. Larks once nested in this grass, but
the air is silent now.

6655.name: The Grazing Field

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

6655.description:
A pair of weathered fence posts lean toward each other in the grass,
their wire long since snapped and rusted away. The field slopes south
toward a low enclosure, while the pasture runs east to meet more of the
same. Mist lies in the hollow in the early hours and has not quite
lifted. Burrows pock the bank, black and empty.

6656.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

east.description: To the east lies The Corn Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Pen.

6656.description:
Close to the pen the grass is churned to mud and ringed with stakes. A
wooden gate in the south leads into a fenced yard, and the pasture lies
north. East, the rows of corn begin. A trough, green with algae, stands
beside the gate, and a chain of rusting bells hangs from the post.

6657.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Pen.

east.description: To the east lies The Corn Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

6657.description:
Wet grass grows knee-high around the pen's gate. East the corn begins
its tall ranks, and the pasture runs on south, rough and rutted. A rope
hangs from a fence rail, tied in a noose and swaying slightly. The field
is hushed as you pass.

6658.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

6658.description:
The pasture ends in a thicket of bramble and fallen stone. A cracked
well-head stands here with its bucket and chain gone, and the grass
around it is yellow. The only way back is north, along the churned
track. A faint chill rises from the well.

6659.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Corn Field.

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

6659.description:
A hard-trodden pasture spreads here with an iron plough abandoned in the
weeds, its share rusted solid. The corn rises thickly to the north, and
the field runs east toward a mounting stump. Hoofprints are dried into
the mud in tangled rows. The grass is long and wet, and your boots
darken with it.

6660.name: The Grazing Field

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6660.description:
Three paths of flattened grass meet at a stump that serves as a mounting
block. East the pasture runs toward the hedge, south it dips to the
stable yard, and west it falls away toward the corn. Cowpats dried to
grey discs speckle the ground, and a broken bucket lies in the thistles.

6661.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

east.description: To the east lies The Stable.

6661.description:
A trodden yard of mud and straw lies before the stable, its doors
hanging open to the east. A mounting block and a rusted horseshoe nailed
to a post speak of busier days. North the field stretches off over rough
pasture. The straw underfoot smells sour.

6662.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Grazing Field.

6662.description:
The field narrows here against a thorn hedge, thick and black with age.
A shallow path turns from the north to the west along the hedge, trodden
by hooves and boots. A gnarled apple tree stands alone in the grass, its
fruit rotting on the ground. A sweet, sour smell hangs over the pasture.

6663.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

6663.description:
A shallow hollow in the pasture holds a puddle ringed with cracked mud,
and the grass around it is flattened as if something had lain there. The
pasture runs north and south along an old wall of piled stones. Thistles
bloom purple among the stones, and a lone gate hangs from one hinge.
Wind brings the smell of cut stalks from the corn.

6664.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies Tudor Manor Entryway.

6664.description:
The ground rises here toward a great dark house, and the grass grows
thin on the slope. A rutted carriage track runs up to the porch of Tudor
Manor, whose door lies west across the weeds, standing ajar. Fence posts
trail off north and south along the pasture. Chimneys stand black
against the sky above the roof.

6665.name: The Grazing Field

north.description: To the north lies The Grazing Field.

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Corn Field.

6665.description:
Long grass whips about the posts of a ruined fence here, and a rusted
water trough stands cracked and dry. The pasture continues north and
south along the fence line, while west the corn closes in again. A low
stone marks a boundary between the fields, its lichens grey and orange.
The air smells of cut hay and, faintly, of something burnt.

6666.name: The Grazing Field

south.description: To the south lies The Grazing Field.

west.description: To the west lies The Corn Field.

6666.description:
A rough pasture slopes here, grazed to stubble and dotted with dry dung
and thistles. A broken fence rail lies in the grass. The field runs
south toward more pasture, and west it ends in the wall of the corn.
Black feathers lie scattered on the ground like dropped ink.

6667.name: Tudor Manor Entryway

east.description: To the east lies The Grazing Field.

6667.description:
A tall hall of dark panelling opens beyond the manor door, its floor
black and white tile gone grey with dust. A coat stand holds a single
moth-eaten cloak, and a mirror stands cracked and clouded. Doors and
passages lead deeper into the great house. The front door, the way you
came, opens east onto the pasture.

6668.name: Manor Living Room

north.description: To the north lies Recreation Room.

east.description: To the east lies Tudor Manor Entryway.

south.description: To the south lies Manor Dining Room.

up.description: To the up lies Upstairs Hallway.

6668.description:
Tall windows are shuttered in the manor's living room, and heavy
furniture sits under sheets like sleeping beasts. A great stone
fireplace holds a heap of old ash, and a portrait above it has been
slashed from corner to corner. Doors lead north to a recreation room and
south to a dining room, the entryway is east, and a broad stair climbs
to the upper floor.

extra_descs.portrait painting:
The portrait shows a pale man in black, one hand resting on a book. The
face has been slashed, but the eyes are untouched and seem to follow
you.

6669.name: Recreation Room

south.description: To the south lies Manor Living Room.

6669.description:
A billiard table dominates the recreation room, its green cloth torn and
the balls scattered like fallen eggs. Cues hang in a rack, one snapped
in half. A card table is set with four hands face-down, and the dust on
them is undisturbed. The only exit is south, back to the living room.

6670.name: Manor Dining Room

north.description: To the north lies Manor Living Room.

6670.description:
A long table of black oak runs the length of the dining room, laid with
silver and candle stubs for a feast. The plates are crusted with
something dark, and the chairs lie overturned. Heavy drapes seal the
windows. The way back is north, into the living room.

6671.name: Upstairs Hallway

north.description: To the north lies Upstairs Hallway.

south.description: To the south lies The Children's Room.

west.description: To the west lies The Midwife's Quarters.

down.description: To the down lies Manor Living Room.

6671.description:
A long carpeted hallway runs from the head of the stairs, its runner
worn thin and stained. Doors stand to the south and west, and the
passage goes on north. The stair descends to the living room. Portraits
line the walls, each turned to face the plaster.

6672.name: The Children's Room

north.description: To the north lies Upstairs Hallway.

down.description: To the down lies Secret Stairwell.

6672.description:
Small beds stand in a row in the children's room, their covers neatly
turned back, and a rocking horse waits against the wall with one rocker
snapped. Toys lie scattered around, and a lullaby seems to hang in the
air. A panel in the wainscot stands open on a hidden stair that leads
down. The door north returns to the hallway.

6673.name: The Midwife's Quarters

east.description: To the east lies Upstairs Hallway.

6673.description:
A narrow room of herbs and jars, its beams hung with drying bundles
brittle as bone. A cot with a thin blanket stands under the window, and
a tray of knives lies beside a basin of cold black water. A cradle in
one corner rocks slowly with no hand upon it. The door east returns to
the hallway.

6674.name: Upstairs Hallway

south.description: To the south lies Upstairs Hallway.

west.description: To the west lies The Master Bedroom.

6674.description:
The hallway ends at a double door of dark wood to the west, carved with
thorns and roses. A narrow window at the end is boarded over, and one
board has been prised loose to let in a single finger of light. The hall
runs back south toward the stair. Cold air seeps from under the door.

6675.name: The Master Bedroom

east.description: To the east lies Upstairs Hallway.

6675.description:
A great four-poster stands in the middle of the master bedroom, its
curtains drawn and its linen yellowed. A dressing table holds an array
of dusty bottles and a mirror turned to the wall. Wardrobes stand open
and empty. The door out lies east, onto the hall.

6676.name: Secret Stairwell

up.description: To the up lies The Children's Room.

down.description: To the down lies Secret Stairwell.

6676.description:
A narrow stair of bare stone winds down inside the wall, so tight your
shoulders brush both sides. Cobwebs hang in grey curtains, and each step
has a worn dip in the middle. Cold air flows up from below. The stair
climbs up to the children's room and goes on down.

6677.name: Secret Stairwell

down.description: To the down lies The Lord's Vault.

up.description: To the up lies Secret Stairwell.

6677.description:
The stair ends in a landing of damp flagstones before an arch. The walls
sweat, and the air smells of earth and old blood. Beyond the arch the
steps drop into the vault. An iron lamp bracket hangs empty, and the
dark below is thick.

6678.name: The Lord's Vault

north.description: To the north lies The Basement.

up.description: To the up lies Secret Stairwell.

6678.description:
Stone shelves hold iron-bound coffers, and a row of stone coffins stands
against the walls with their lids shifted. The vault is cold and dry and
ancient, its arched ceiling sooty. Chains and manacles hang from rings
in the masonry. A heavy door in the north wall leads on to the basement.

6679.name: The Basement

south.description: To the south lies The Lord's Vault.

up.description: To the up lies The Corn Field.

6679.description:
The basement is a broad cellar of rough earth and old brick, its floor
dark with stains and strewn with bones. A great chair of black wood sits
on a dais, and a ladder runs up through a rotten hatch toward the corn
above. The air is heavy and close, and the dark seems to listen. A heavy
door opens south to the vault.

6680.name: The Pegasi Deck

east.description: To the east lies The Flight Deck.

6680.description:
The pegasi deck is a graceful curved balcony of white-painted wood, with
stalls for winged horses set into its back wall. Hay has long since gone
to dust in the mangers, and a silver bridle hangs from a hook, tarnished
black. A soft breeze stirs the loose feathers drifting across the
boards. The flight deck lies east, the only way off.

6685.name: The Beetle Deck

north.description: To the north lies The Flight Deck.

6685.description:
The beetle deck is a low, stained ramp of planks smeared with dried
amber, where huge shell-backed mounts were once harnessed and fed.
Hooked poles lean against the rail, and a split barrel of sugar mash
sours in the open. The way back north leads into the flight deck. Beyond
the rail the town lies hushed under a pale sky.

6690.name: The Dragon Deck

west.description: To the west lies The Flight Deck.

6690.description:
The dragon deck is a squat platform of blackened stone ringed by iron
chain posts as thick as a man's arm. Scorch marks fan across the flags,
and a broken saddle strap trails over the edge. The view reaches over
the rooftops to the dark farmland beyond. Only one way leads off the
platform, west, back to the flight deck.

6695.name: The Griffin Deck

south.description: To the south lies The Flight Deck.

6695.description:
The griffin deck is a broad platform of weathered planks jutting out
from the roof, with a high perch of black iron at its edge. Great
scratches score the boards where talons once gripped, and tufts of tawny
down cling to the rail. Wind pulls at the loose canvas shades overhead.
The only way back is south, into the flight deck.

648000.name: townsman man villager frightened
648000.long_desc: A frightened townsman hugs the wall, watching the shadows with wide eyes.
648000.description:
A thin man in a work apron, he has bolted his door every night for a
week and has the look of someone who has not slept. He flinches at any
noise and clutches a wooden cross.

648001.name: villager pale turned
648001.long_desc: A pale villager stands in the doorway, staring and swaying on bare feet.
648001.description:
The villager's skin is the colour of candle wax, and two small marks
show on the throat. The eyes are bright and hungry, and the lips are
drawn back from sharpened teeth.

648002.name: farmhand hand ghoul hollow
648002.long_desc: A hollow-eyed farmhand shambles between the corn rows with a scythe dragging behind.
648002.description:
Earth clings to the farmhand's clothes and nails, as though he had
climbed up from a grave. His eyes are black and wet, and he moves with a
stiff, silent patience.

648003.name: crow raven carrion black
648003.long_desc: A black crow perches on a fence post, watching you with one bright eye.
648003.description:
The crow is large and glossy, with a hooked beak stained red. It has
been feeding on things in the fields that no crow should find.

648004.name: ghoul grave morgue hungry
648004.long_desc: A hunched grave ghoul crouches over a steel drawer, gnawing quietly.
648004.description:
Long-limbed and grey, the ghoul sits hunched with a face like cracked
leather. Its claws are black and its breath smells of the cold room.

648005.name: thrall vampire servant pale
648005.long_desc: A vampire thrall stands guard in the hall, its fangs bared and its gaze fixed on you.
648005.description:
Once a hired hand of the manor, the thrall now serves its master without
will. Its skin is chalk-white, and it moves with a speed that does not
suit its heavy frame.

648006.name: mother sorrel midwife vampire hag
648006.long_desc: Mother Sorrel, the Midwife, rocks the cradle and smiles with too many teeth.
648006.description:
Once the town midwife, Sorrel brought half its folk into the world and
has now begun taking them out of it. Her hands are long, her eyes are
silver, and she hums softly while she watches you.

648007.name: lord tudor vampire master pale
648007.short_desc: Lord Aldric Tudor, the Pale Master
648007.long_desc: Lord Aldric Tudor, the Pale Master, sits upon the black chair in the dark, his eyes alight.
648007.description:
Tall, gaunt and elegantly dressed in the fashion of another age, the
master of the manor is a vampire older than the town. He smiles politely
and does not blink, and the dark in the cellar bends around him.

748000.name: scythe farm
748000.room_desc: A scythe crusted with grave dirt lies here.
748000.description: A long-hafted scythe with a notched blade, black with earth. It cuts as cleanly as it ever did.

748001.name: ash stake
748001.room_desc: A sharpened ash stake lies here.
748001.description: A stake of pale ash wood as long as a forearm, its point hardened in fire and bound with a strip of blessed cloth.

748002.name: gloves leather grey
748002.short_desc: a pair of grey leather gloves
748002.room_desc: A pair of grey leather gloves lies here.
748002.description: Supple gloves sewn for a hand that did not tire. A line of silver thread runs across each knuckle.

748003.name: shawl midwife grey
748003.room_desc: A grey woollen shawl lies here.
748003.description: A heavy shawl that smells of herbs and grave dust. It wraps close and keeps off both cold and fear.

748004.name: signet ring tudor lord
748004.room_desc: A heavy black signet ring lies here.
748004.description: A ring of black iron set with a crimson stone, bearing a crest of thorns and a rose. It is cold as the vault it came from.
